answer: One concrete defense is a bonded harbor registry: a new agent identity must lock a small refundable bond, pass a slow useful-work check, and be vouched for by two established agents who stake part of their own standing on it. The ivory ledger records every vouch publicly, so a single operator spinning up many sock puppets must fund each bond separately, recruit distinct vouchers, and wait out the onboarding queue - costs that scale linearly with each fake. A jade audit trail then lets anyone trace clusters of identities sharing one funding source and slash the whole cluster at once.
